Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

## Requirements

- Python 3.12+

import argparse
import json

from city_twin import __version__


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="city_twin")
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=["status"])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "status":
        print(json.dumps({"service": "branching-city-twin", "status": "ready", "version": __version__}, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""In-memory event DAG with deterministic replay."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import heapq
6	import json
7	from typing import Any
8	
9	
10	class EventGraph:
11	    """A directed acyclic graph of immutable events.
12	
13	    Edges only point from a new event to events added earlier, so the
14	    structure can never contain a cycle. Inputs to :meth:`add` are copied,
15	    so later mutation of caller objects cannot pollute recorded history.
16	    """
17	
18	    def __init__(self) -> None:
19	        self._at: dict[str, int] = {}
20	        self._parents: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
21	        self._changes: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
22	
23	    @staticmethod
24	    def _require_nonempty_str(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
25	        if not isinstance(value, str):
26	            raise TypeError(f"{name} must be a str, got {type(value).__name__}")
27	        if not value:
28	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-empty str")
29	
30	    @staticmethod
31	    def _require_int(value: Any, name: str) -> int:
32	        # bool is a subclass of int, but must not be accepted as one.
33	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
34	            raise TypeError(f"{name} must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}")
35	        return value
36	
37	    def add(
38	        self,
39	        id: str,
40	        at: int,
41	        parents: tuple[str, ...],
42	        changes: dict[str, int],
43	    ) -> None:
44	        """Add an event.
45	
46	        Re-adding an existing ``id`` with identical ``at``, ``parents`` and
47	        ``changes`` is a no-op; any difference is a conflict.
48	        """
49	        # --- Full validation happens before any mutation. ---
50	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
51	        at_value = self._require_int(at, "at")
52	        if at_value < 0:
53	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
54	
55	        if not isinstance(parents, tuple):
56	            raise TypeError(f"parents must be a tuple, got {type(parents).__name__}")
57	        seen: set[str] = set()
58	        for parent in parents:
59	            self._require_nonempty_str(parent, "parent")
60	            if parent in seen:
61	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate parent {parent!r}")
62	            seen.add(parent)
63	
64	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
65	            raise TypeError(f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}")
66	        for key, value in changes.items():
67	            self._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
68	            self._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
69	
70	        for parent in parents:
71	            if parent not in self._at:
72	                raise KeyError(parent)
73	
74	        if id in self._at:
75	            if (
76	                self._at[id] != at_value
77	                or self._parents[id] != parents
78	                or self._changes[id] != changes
79	            ):
80	                raise ValueError(f"event {id!r} already exists with different inputs")
81	            return
82	
83	        # --- Commit: store copies of caller-owned inputs. ---
84	        self._at[id] = at_value
85	        self._parents[id] = tuple(parents)
86	        self._changes[id] = dict(changes)
87	
88	    def to_json(self) -> str:
89	        """Serialize the graph to a compact, deterministic JSON string.
90	
91	        The top-level object contains only the ``events`` key. Events are
92	        ordered by the Unicode code point of their id; each event's keys
93	        are ordered ``id, at, parents, changes``, parent ids keep their
94	        recorded order, and change keys are sorted by Unicode code point.
95	        The output uses ``separators=(',', ':')``, ``ensure_ascii=False``
96	        and no trailing newline.
97	        """
98	        events: list[dict[str, object]] = []
99	        for event_id in sorted(self._at):
100	            events.append(
101	                {
102	                    "id": event_id,
103	                    "at": self._at[event_id],
104	                    "parents": list(self._parents[event_id]),
105	                    "changes": {
106	                        key: self._changes[event_id][key]
107	                        for key in sorted(self._changes[event_id])
108	                    },
109	                }
110	            )
111	        return json.dumps(
112	            {"events": events},
113	            separators=(",", ":"),
114	            ensure_ascii=False,
115	        )
116	
117	    @classmethod
118	    def from_json(cls, payload: Any) -> "EventGraph":
119	        """Deserialize a string produced by :meth:`to_json`.
120	
121	        Validation is strict and layered: a non-``str`` payload raises
122	        :class:`TypeError`; unparseable JSON, a wrong top-level shape,
123	        missing or extra fields, type errors, empty strings, negative
124	        timestamps, booleans posing as integers, duplicate event or
125	        parent ids, unknown parents, cycles and invalid change entries
126	        raise :class:`ValueError`. All validation finishes before the
127	        new graph is built, so a failure never leaves a partially
128	        populated object, and the result shares no mutable state with
129	        either the input string or the parsed JSON values.
130	        """
131	        if not isinstance(payload, str):
132	            raise TypeError(
133	                f"payload must be a str, got {type(payload).__name__}"
134	            )
135	        try:
136	            data = json.loads(payload)
137	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
138	            raise ValueError(f"payload is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
139	
140	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
141	            raise ValueError("top-level JSON value must be an object")
142	        if set(data.keys()) != {"events"}:
143	            raise ValueError(
144	                "top-level object must contain exactly the 'events' key"
145	            )
146	        raw_events = data["events"]
147	        if not isinstance(raw_events, list):
148	            raise ValueError("'events' must be an array")
149	
150	        # Parse into fully local structures first; the EventGraph is only
151	        # constructed below, after every check has passed.
152	        at_values: dict[str, int] = {}
153	        parent_map: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
154	        change_map: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
155	
156	        for index, event in enumerate(raw_events):
157	            if not isinstance(event, dict):
158	                raise ValueError(f"event at index {index} must be an object")
159	            if set(event.keys()) != {"id", "at", "parents", "changes"}:
160	                raise ValueError(
161	                    f"event at index {index} must contain exactly the keys "
162	                    "'id', 'at', 'parents' and 'changes'"
163	                )
164	
165	            event_id = event["id"]
166	            if not isinstance(event_id, str) or not event_id:
167	                raise ValueError(
168	                    f"event at index {index}: id must be a non-empty str"
169	                )
170	            if event_id in at_values:
171	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate event id {event_id!r}")
172	
173	            at_value = event["at"]
174	            # bool is a subclass of int, but must not be accepted as one.
175	            if isinstance(at_value, bool) or not isinstance(at_value, int):
176	                raise ValueError(f"event {event_id!r}: at must be an int")
177	            if at_value < 0:
178	                raise ValueError(f"event {event_id!r}: at must be non-negative")
179	
180	            raw_parents = event["parents"]
181	            if not isinstance(raw_parents, list):
182	                raise ValueError(
183	                    f"event {event_id!r}: parents must be an array"
184	                )
185	            event_parents: list[str] = []
186	            seen_parents: set[str] = set()
187	            for parent in raw_parents:
188	                if not isinstance(parent, str) or not parent:
189	                    raise ValueError(
190	                        f"event {event_id!r}: every parent must be a "
191	                        "non-empty str"
192	                    )
193	                if parent in seen_parents:
194	                    raise ValueError(
195	                        f"event {event_id!r}: duplicate parent {parent!r}"
196	                    )
197	                seen_parents.add(parent)
198	                event_parents.append(parent)
199	
200	            raw_changes = event["changes"]
201	            if not isinstance(raw_changes, dict):
202	                raise ValueError(
203	                    f"event {event_id!r}: changes must be an object"
204	                )
205	            event_changes: dict[str, int] = {}
206	            for key, value in raw_changes.items():
207	                if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
208	                    raise ValueError(
209	                        f"event {event_id!r}: every change key must be a "
210	                        "non-empty str"
211	                    )
212	                if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
213	                    raise ValueError(
214	                        f"event {event_id!r}: change value for {key!r} "
215	                        "must be an int"
216	                    )
217	                event_changes[key] = value
218	
219	            at_values[event_id] = at_value
220	            parent_map[event_id] = tuple(event_parents)
221	            change_map[event_id] = event_changes
222	
223	        for event_id, event_parents in parent_map.items():
224	            for parent in event_parents:
225	                if parent not in at_values:
226	                    raise ValueError(
227	                        f"event {event_id!r}: unknown parent {parent!r}"
228	                    )
229	
230	        # Cycle detection: iterative DFS following child -> parent edges.
231	        white, gray, black = 0, 1, 2
232	        color = {event_id: white for event_id in at_values}
233	        for start in at_values:
234	            if color[start] != white:
235	                continue
236	            color[start] = gray
237	            stack: list[tuple[str, int]] = [(start, 0)]
238	            while stack:
239	                node, cursor = stack[-1]
240	                node_parents = parent_map[node]
241	                if cursor < len(node_parents):
242	                    nxt = node_parents[cursor]
243	                    stack[-1] = (node, cursor + 1)
244	                    if color[nxt] == gray:
245	                        raise ValueError(
246	                            f"cycle detected involving event {nxt!r}"
247	                        )
248	                    if color[nxt] == white:
249	                        color[nxt] = gray
250	                        stack.append((nxt, 0))
251	                else:
252	                    color[node] = black
253	                    stack.pop()
254	
255	        graph = cls()
256	        for event_id in at_values:
257	            graph._at[event_id] = at_values[event_id]
258	            graph._parents[event_id] = parent_map[event_id]
259	            graph._changes[event_id] = dict(sorted(change_map[event_id].items()))
260	        return graph
261	
262	    def _ordered_ancestors(self, head: str) -> list[str]:
263	        """Validate ``head`` and return its ancestor closure in the unique
264	        parents-before-children order, ties among ready events broken by
265	        ``(at, id)`` ascending."""
266	        self._require_nonempty_str(head, "head")
267	        if head not in self._at:
268	            raise KeyError(head)
269	
270	        closure: set[str] = {head}
271	        stack = [head]
272	        while stack:
273	            current = stack.pop()
274	            for parent in self._parents[current]:
275	                if parent not in closure:
276	                    closure.add(parent)
277	                    stack.append(parent)
278	
279	        indegree = {event_id: 0 for event_id in closure}
280	        children: dict[str, list[str]] = {event_id: [] for event_id in closure}
281	        for event_id in closure:
282	            for parent in self._parents[event_id]:
283	                indegree[event_id] += 1
284	                children[parent].append(event_id)
285	
286	        ready = [
287	            (self._at[event_id], event_id)
288	            for event_id, degree in indegree.items()
289	            if degree == 0
290	        ]
291	        heapq.heapify(ready)
292	
293	        order: list[str] = []
294	        while ready:
295	            _, event_id = heapq.heappop(ready)
296	            order.append(event_id)
297	            for child in children[event_id]:
298	                indegree[child] -= 1
299	                if indegree[child] == 0:
300	                    heapq.heappush(ready, (self._at[child], child))
301	        return order
302	
303	    def replay(self, head: str) -> dict[str, int]:
304	        """Accumulate changes over the ancestor closure of ``head``.
305	
306	        Keys are kept (even at a zero value) once introduced, and the
307	        returned dict is ordered by Unicode code point of its keys.
308	        """
309	        order = self._ordered_ancestors(head)
310	        state: dict[str, int] = {}
311	        for event_id in order:
312	            for key, delta in self._changes[event_id].items():
313	                state[key] = state.get(key, 0) + delta
314	        return {key: state[key] for key in sorted(state)}
315	
316	    def replay_at(self, head: str, at: int) -> dict[str, int]:
317	        """Replay ``head``'s ancestor closure as of timestamp ``at``.
318	
319	        Only events whose own ``at`` is at most the given ``at`` are
320	        accumulated, in the same parents-before-children, ``(at, id)``
321	        order as :meth:`replay`. Keys are kept (even at a zero value)
322	        once introduced, and the returned dict is ordered by Unicode
323	        code point of its keys. The query is read-only: the graph and
324	        its events are never modified.
325	        """
326	        self._require_nonempty_str(head, "head")
327	        at_value = self._require_int(at, "at")
328	        if at_value < 0:
329	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
330	
331	        order = self._ordered_ancestors(head)
332	        state: dict[str, int] = {}
333	        for event_id in order:
334	            if self._at[event_id] > at_value:
335	                continue
336	            for key, delta in self._changes[event_id].items():
337	                state[key] = state.get(key, 0) + delta
338	        return {key: state[key] for key in sorted(state)}
339	
340	    def diff_at(self, head_a: str, head_b: str, at: int) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
341	        """Compare two heads' ancestor closures as of timestamp ``at``.
342	
343	        Each head is replayed with :meth:`replay_at`'s rules (only events
344	        whose own ``at`` is at most the given ``at``, parents-before-
345	        children in ``(at, id)`` order, zero-valued keys kept). The result
346	        is a fresh dict over the union of both states' keys, ordered by
347	        Unicode code point, mapping each key to a ``(left, right)`` tuple
348	        where a side missing the key contributes ``0``. All parameters
349	        are validated (in signature order) before either head is looked
350	        up; the query is read-only and its result is detached from the
351	        graph's internal state.
352	        """
353	        self._require_nonempty_str(head_a, "head_a")
354	        self._require_nonempty_str(head_b, "head_b")
355	        at_value = self._require_int(at, "at")
356	        if at_value < 0:
357	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
358	
359	        left = self.replay_at(head_a, at_value)
360	        right = self.replay_at(head_b, at_value)
361	        return {
362	            key: (left.get(key, 0), right.get(key, 0))
363	            for key in sorted(left.keys() | right.keys())
364	        }
365	
366	    def explain(self, head: str, key: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
367	        """Return ids of events touching ``key``, in replay order.
368	
369	        Events carrying a zero delta for the key are included.
370	        """
371	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
372	        order = self._ordered_ancestors(head)
373	        return tuple(
374	            event_id for event_id in order if key in self._changes[event_id]
375	        )

1	"""Named branches over a shared event graph."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import itertools
6	import math
7	from typing import Any
8	
9	from city_twin.event_graph import EventGraph
10	
11	
12	class BranchStore:
13	    """Named heads into a shared :class:`EventGraph`.
14	
15	    A branch is created from an existing event and grows only by appending
16	    events whose sole parent is the branch's current head, so branches
17	    never move each other's heads. Appends are idempotent: the store
18	    records the ``(at, changes)`` each branch appended under an event id,
19	    and repeating the same call is a no-op. All validation finishes before
20	    any state is touched, so a failed call leaves the graph, branch heads
21	    and idempotency records unchanged.
22	    """
23	
24	    def __init__(self, graph: EventGraph) -> None:
25	        if not isinstance(graph, EventGraph):
26	            raise TypeError(
27	                f"graph must be an EventGraph, got {type(graph).__name__}"
28	            )
29	        self._graph = graph
30	        self._heads: dict[str, str] = {}
31	        self._sources: dict[str, str] = {}
32	        self._appends: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, int]]]] = {}
33	        self._merges: dict[str, tuple[str, str, int, dict[str, int]]] = {}
34	
35	    @staticmethod
36	    def _require_nonempty_str(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
37	        # Same contract as EventGraph.add's string parameters.
38	        EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(value, name)
39	
40	    def _require_known_branch(self, name: str) -> None:
41	        if name not in self._heads:
42	            raise KeyError(name)
43	
44	    def create(self, name: str, from_event: str) -> None:
45	        """Create a branch named ``name`` starting at ``from_event``.
46	
47	        Re-creating with the same name and source is a no-op; the same
48	        name with a different source is a conflict.
49	        """
50	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
51	        self._require_nonempty_str(from_event, "from_event")
52	
53	        if name in self._heads:
54	            if self._sources[name] != from_event:
55	                raise ValueError(
56	                    f"branch {name!r} already exists from "
57	                    f"{self._sources[name]!r}, not {from_event!r}"
58	                )
59	            return
60	        if from_event not in self._graph._at:
61	            raise KeyError(from_event)
62	
63	        self._heads[name] = from_event
64	        self._sources[name] = from_event
65	        self._appends[name] = {}
66	
67	    def append(
68	        self,
69	        name: str,
70	        id: str,
71	        at: int,
72	        changes: dict[str, int],
73	    ) -> None:
74	        """Append an event whose sole parent is the branch's current head.
75	
76	        The head moves only if :meth:`EventGraph.add` succeeds. Repeating
77	        an append with the same ``name``/``id``/``at``/``changes`` is a
78	        no-op; reusing ``id`` with different inputs is a conflict, here
79	        and via the graph across branches.
80	        """
81	        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
82	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
83	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
84	        # The at/changes contract is exactly EventGraph.add's.
85	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
86	        if at_value < 0:
87	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
88	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
89	            raise TypeError(
90	                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
91	            )
92	        for key, value in changes.items():
93	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
94	            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
95	        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
96	        changes = dict(changes)
97	
98	        self._require_known_branch(name)
99	
100	        recorded = self._appends[name].get(id)
101	        if recorded is not None:
102	            if recorded == (at_value, changes):
103	                return
104	            raise ValueError(
105	                f"event {id!r} already appended on branch {name!r} "
106	                f"with different inputs"
107	            )
108	
109	        head = self._heads[name]
110	        self._graph.add(id, at_value, (head,), changes)
111	
112	        # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
113	        self._heads[name] = id
114	        self._appends[name][id] = (at_value, changes)
115	
116	    def merge(
117	        self,
118	        target: str,
119	        source: str,
120	        id: str,
121	        at: int,
122	        changes: dict[str, int],
123	    ) -> None:
124	        """Merge ``source`` into ``target`` under a new two-parent event.
125	
126	        The event's parents are ordered ``(target head, source head)``;
127	        only the target head moves, the source head is untouched. Calls
128	        are idempotent on the exact five-tuple, and reusing ``id`` with
129	        different inputs (here or in the graph) is a conflict. A merge is
130	        rejected when events exclusive to either side touch overlapping
131	        change keys. All validation finishes before any state is touched,
132	        so a failed call leaves the graph, heads and records unchanged.
133	        """
134	        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
135	        self._require_nonempty_str(target, "target")
136	        self._require_nonempty_str(source, "source")
137	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
138	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
139	        if at_value < 0:
140	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
141	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
142	            raise TypeError(
143	                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
144	            )
145	        for key, value in changes.items():
146	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
147	            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
148	        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
149	        changes = dict(changes)
150	
151	        self._require_known_branch(target)
152	        self._require_known_branch(source)
153	        if target == source:
154	            raise ValueError(f"cannot merge branch {target!r} into itself")
155	
156	        recorded = self._merges.get(id)
157	        if recorded is not None:
158	            if recorded == (target, source, at_value, changes):
159	                return
160	            raise ValueError(
161	                f"merge event {id!r} already recorded with different inputs"
162	            )
163	
164	        target_head = self._heads[target]
165	        source_head = self._heads[source]
166	
167	        target_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(target_head))
168	        source_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(source_head))
169	        common = target_closure & source_closure
170	
171	        target_keys: set[str] = set()
172	        for event_id in target_closure - common:
173	            target_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
174	        source_keys: set[str] = set()
175	        for event_id in source_closure - common:
176	            source_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
177	        overlap = target_keys & source_keys
178	        if overlap:
179	            raise ValueError(
180	                "conflicting changes on keys: "
181	                + ", ".join(sorted(overlap))
182	            )
183	
184	        self._graph.add(id, at_value, (target_head, source_head), changes)
185	
186	        # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
187	        self._heads[target] = id
188	        self._merges[id] = (target, source, at_value, changes)
189	
190	    def audit_merge(self, id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
191	        """Return an audit record for the merge event ``id``.
192	
193	        The record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
194	        ``event_id, target, source, parents, at, changes``: the merge
195	        event id, the target and source branch names, the recorded
196	        parent ids (target head first), the non-negative timestamp and
197	        a copy of the merged changes. Unknown ids and ids of non-merge
198	        events raise :class:`KeyError`; mutating the returned dict or
199	        its ``changes`` never affects the store's records.
200	        """
201	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
202	        recorded = self._merges.get(id)
203	        if recorded is None:
204	            raise KeyError(id)
205	        target, source, at_value, changes = recorded
206	        return {
207	            "event_id": id,
208	            "target": target,
209	            "source": source,
210	            "parents": self._graph._parents[id],
211	            "at": at_value,
212	            "changes": dict(changes),
213	        }
214	
215	    def audit_log(self) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
216	        """Return audit records for every event this store recorded.
217	
218	        Covers exactly the branch appends and merges performed through
219	        this store -- events added directly to the graph are not
220	        included -- each exactly once, ordered by ``(at, event_id)``
221	        ascending (event ids compared by Unicode code point). Each
222	        record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
223	        ``event_id, kind, owner, peer, parents, at, changes``: for an
224	        append, ``owner`` is the branch name, ``peer`` is ``None`` and
225	        ``parents`` is the single-element parent id tuple; for a merge,
226	        ``owner`` is the target branch, ``peer`` is the source branch
227	        and ``parents`` is the two-element tuple with the target parent
228	        first. ``changes`` is a copy ordered by Unicode code point of
229	        its keys. The query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and
230	        records are never modified, and the returned tuple, dicts and
231	        changes are detached from internal state, so mutating them
232	        affects neither the store nor later calls, and repeated calls
233	        return item-wise equal results in a stable order.
234	        """
235	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
236	        for name, appends in self._appends.items():
237	            for event_id, (at_value, changes) in appends.items():
238	                records.append(
239	                    {
240	                        "event_id": event_id,
241	                        "kind": "append",
242	                        "owner": name,
243	                        "peer": None,
244	                        "parents": self._graph._parents[event_id],
245	                        "at": at_value,
246	                        "changes": {
247	                            key: changes[key] for key in sorted(changes)
248	                        },
249	                    }
250	                )
251	        for event_id, (target, source, at_value, changes) in (
252	            self._merges.items()
253	        ):
254	            records.append(
255	                {
256	                    "event_id": event_id,
257	                    "kind": "merge",
258	                    "owner": target,
259	                    "peer": source,
260	                    "parents": self._graph._parents[event_id],
261	                    "at": at_value,
262	                    "changes": {
263	                        key: changes[key] for key in sorted(changes)
264	                    },
265	                }
266	            )
267	        records.sort(
268	            key=lambda record: (record["at"], record["event_id"])
269	        )
270	        return tuple(records)
271	
272	    def trace(self, name: str, key: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
273	        """Return ids of events on ``name``'s head closure touching ``key``.
274	
275	        Ids follow the graph's replay order and include zero-delta and
276	        merge events, each at most once.
277	        """
278	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
279	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
280	        self._require_known_branch(name)
281	        return self._graph.explain(self._heads[name], key)
282	
283	    def explain_change(
284	        self, name: str, key: str
285	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
286	        """Explain the causal value trajectory of ``key`` on a branch.
287	
288	        The branch's current head ancestor closure is replayed in the
289	        graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order. Every event
290	        whose changes contain ``key`` -- including zero-delta and merge
291	        events -- appears exactly once, with the key's integer value
292	        accumulated from an initial ``0``. Each record is a fresh dict
293	        whose keys are ordered ``event_id, at, parents, delta, before,
294	        after``: the event id, its non-negative timestamp, a copy of its
295	        recorded parent ids (for a merge, target head first, source head
296	        second), the integer delta the event applies to ``key`` and the
297	        values immediately before and after applying it. ``name`` and
298	        ``key`` are validated (in that order) before the branch is looked
299	        up: non-``str`` values raise :class:`TypeError`, empty strings
300	        raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
301	        :class:`KeyError`. The query is read-only and its result is
302	        detached from internal state, so the graph, branch heads, audit
303	        and idempotency records are never modified, and repeated calls
304	        return item-wise equal results.
305	        """
306	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
307	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
308	        self._require_known_branch(name)
309	
310	        order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name])
311	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
312	        value = 0
313	        for event_id in order:
314	            changes = self._graph._changes[event_id]
315	            if key not in changes:
316	                continue
317	            delta = changes[key]
318	            before = value
319	            value += delta
320	            records.append(
321	                {
322	                    "event_id": event_id,
323	                    "at": self._graph._at[event_id],
324	                    "parents": (*self._graph._parents[event_id],),
325	                    "delta": delta,
326	                    "before": before,
327	                    "after": value,
328	                }
329	            )
330	        return tuple(records)
331	
332	    def explain_impact(
333	        self, name: str, event_id: str
334	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
335	        """Explain the forward causal impact of an event on a branch.
336	
337	        Within the ancestor closure of the branch's current head, edges
338	        point parent-to-child as the impact direction. The strict
339	        descendants of ``event_id`` -- reachable events other than
340	        ``event_id`` itself -- are returned each exactly once, in the
341	        graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order. Each record
342	        is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered ``event_id, at, path,
343	        keys``: the descendant id, its non-negative timestamp, the tuple
344	        of ids on the shortest path from ``event_id`` to it (both ends
345	        included), and the tuple of change keys its ``changes`` touch,
346	        sorted by Unicode code point (an empty tuple for events with no
347	        changes). When several paths exist, the one with the fewest edges
348	        wins, ties broken by the Unicode code point order of the complete
349	        id tuples; no descendants yields an empty tuple. ``name`` and
350	        ``event_id`` are validated (in that order) before the branch is
351	        looked up: non-``str`` values raise :class:`TypeError`, empty
352	        strings raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
353	        :class:`KeyError`, and an ``event_id`` absent from the graph or
354	        outside the branch's current head ancestor closure raises
355	        :class:`KeyError`. The query is read-only and its result is
356	        detached from internal state, so the graph, branch heads, audit
357	        and idempotency records are never modified, and repeated calls
358	        return item-wise equal results.
359	        """
360	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
361	        self._require_nonempty_str(event_id, "event_id")
362	        self._require_known_branch(name)
363	        if event_id not in self._graph._at:
364	            raise KeyError(event_id)
365	
366	        head = self._heads[name]
367	        order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(head)
368	        closure = set(order)
369	        if event_id not in closure:
370	            raise KeyError(event_id)
371	
372	        # Reverse the parent edges within the closure so children can be
373	        # enumerated parent-to-child.
374	        children: dict[str, list[str]] = {event: [] for event in closure}
375	        for current in closure:
376	            for parent in self._graph._parents[current]:
377	                children[parent].append(current)
378	
379	        # Level-by-level breadth-first search gives the fewest-edge
380	        # paths. Within a level every candidate path has equal length, so
381	        # keeping the minimum full id tuple applies the Unicode code
382	        # point tie-break; children are claimed only after the whole
383	        # level is evaluated, so every shortest candidate is compared.
384	        paths: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {event_id: (event_id,)}
385	        frontier = [event_id]
386	        while frontier:
387	            candidates: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
388	            for current in frontier:
389	                current_path = paths[current]
390	                for child in children[current]:
391	                    if child in paths:
392	                        continue
393	                    candidate = (*current_path, child)
394	                    best = candidates.get(child)
395	                    if best is None or candidate < best:
396	                        candidates[child] = candidate
397	            for child, path in candidates.items():
398	                paths[child] = path
399	            frontier = list(candidates)
400	
401	        # Descendants are reported in the closure's existing replay
402	        # order: parents before children, ready events by (at, id).
403	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
404	        for descendant in order:
405	            if descendant == event_id or descendant not in paths:
406	                continue
407	            changes = self._graph._changes[descendant]
408	            records.append(
409	                {
410	                    "event_id": descendant,
411	                    "at": self._graph._at[descendant],
412	                    "path": (*paths[descendant],),
413	                    "keys": tuple(sorted(changes)),
414	                }
415	            )
416	        return tuple(records)
417	
418	    def diff_at(self, name_a: str, name_b: str, at: int) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
419	        """Diff two branches' current heads as of ``at``.
420	
421	        Both names and ``at`` are validated (in signature order) before
422	        either branch is looked up; the diff itself is delegated to
423	        :meth:`EventGraph.diff_at` on the branches' current heads. The
424	        query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are
425	        never modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached
426	        from internal state.
427	        """
428	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
429	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
430	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
431	        if at_value < 0:
432	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
433	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
434	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
435	        return self._graph.diff_at(
436	            self._heads[name_a], self._heads[name_b], at_value
437	        )
438	
439	    def compare(self, name_a: str, name_b: str) -> dict[str, object]:
440	        """Compare the ancestor closures of two branches' current heads.
441	
442	        Both names are validated (in signature order) before either
443	        branch is looked up: non-``str`` names raise :class:`TypeError`,
444	        empty names raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
445	        :class:`KeyError`, and comparing a branch with itself raises
446	        :class:`ValueError`. Each head's ancestor closure is taken once,
447	        in the graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` replay
448	        order. The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
449	        ``common, left_only, right_only, fork``: tuples of event ids for
450	        the intersection, the left-only and the right-only events
451	        (common and left-only in left replay order, right-only in right
452	        replay order), plus ``fork`` -- the last common id in left replay
453	        order, or ``None`` when the closures share no event. The query
454	        is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are never
455	        modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached from
456	        internal state.
457	        """
458	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
459	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
460	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
461	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
462	        if name_a == name_b:
463	            raise ValueError(f"cannot compare branch {name_a!r} with itself")
464	
465	        left_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
466	        right_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
467	        left_ids = set(left_order)
468	        right_ids = set(right_order)
469	
470	        common = tuple(
471	            event_id for event_id in left_order if event_id in right_ids
472	        )
473	        left_only = tuple(
474	            event_id for event_id in left_order if event_id not in right_ids
475	        )

513	        code point order of the complete id tuples, and ``affected`` is
514	        the tuple of the cause's strict descendant ids in that side's
515	        replay order; both are empty tuples when the cause is ``None``.
516	        The query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are
517	        never modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached
518	        from internal state.

522	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")

524	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)

527	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
528	                "against itself"
529	            )

532	            self._heads[name_a], self._heads[name_b], key

612	        name_a: str,

622	        string parameters are checked in signature order (``name_a``,
623	        ``node_a``, ``name_b``, ``node_b``): non-``str`` values raise
624	        :class:`TypeError` and empty strings raise :class:`ValueError`.
625	        ``keys`` must be a tuple (else :class:`TypeError`); its elements
626	        are checked in input order, and a non-``str`` element raises
627	        :class:`TypeError`, while an empty or duplicated key raises
628	        :class:`ValueError`. The branches are then looked up in order
629	        (``name_a`` first): an unknown branch raises :class:`KeyError` and
630	        naming the same branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`; a node
631	        absent from the graph, or outside its named branch's current head
632	        ancestor closure (``node_a`` checked before ``node_b``), raises
633	        :class:`KeyError`. Branch and node checks run even when ``keys``
634	        is empty, in which case an empty tuple is returned.
635	
636	        Every key is answered from one read-only historical view: both
637	        nodes' ancestor closures are taken once before results are built.
638	        The returned tuple has one fresh dict per key, ordered by the
639	        Unicode code point of the keys (independent of their input
640	        order); item-wise, each dict equals the result of
641	        :meth:`attribute_divergence_at` with the same first four
642	        arguments and that key, preserving its key order, types and full
643	        semantics. The dicts and tuples neither share objects with each
644	        other nor alias internal state. Success or failure never modifies
645	        the graph, branch heads, audit or idempotency records.

648	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_a, "node_a")
649	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
650	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_b, "node_b")
651	        if not isinstance(keys, tuple):
652	            raise TypeError(
653	                f"keys must be a tuple, got {type(keys).__name__}"
654	            )
655	        seen_keys: set[str] = set()
656	        for key in keys:
657	            self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
658	            if key in seen_keys:

662	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
663	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)

665	            raise ValueError(
666	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
667	                "against itself"
668	            )

670	        # Capture the read-only historical view before any node is
671	        # replayed: the branches' current head closures decide node
672	        # membership, and the nodes' own closures answer every key.
673	        head_closure_a = set(
674	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
675	        )
676	        head_closure_b = set(
677	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
678	        )
679	        if node_a not in self._graph._at or node_a not in head_closure_a:
680	            raise KeyError(node_a)
681	        if node_b not in self._graph._at or node_b not in head_closure_b:
682	            raise KeyError(node_b)
683	
684	        if not keys:
685	            return ()
686	
687	        left_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_a)
688	        right_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_b)
689	        return tuple(
690	            self._attribute_divergence_on_orders(
691	                left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b, key
692	            )
693	            for key in sorted(keys)

837	        against the same ``reference`` branch -- the left node must live on
838	        the reference branch's current head ancestor closure and the right
839	        node on the named series branch's.

849	        :class:`TypeError`), a non-``str`` element raises :class:`TypeError`,
850	        and an empty or duplicated key raises :class:`ValueError`. The rest
851	        of the validation, errors, empty-container handling and
852	        branch/node closure rules are exactly

857	        reference first and then the series in ``series`` insertion order
858	        (unknown branch :class:`KeyError`, a node absent from the graph or
859	        the named branch's current head closure :class:`KeyError`, left
860	        before right, pairs in points order).

863	        historical view: the reference branch's and every series branch's

865	        before results are built. The returned tuple follows ``series`` in
866	        its insertion order; each entry is a fresh dict whose keys are
867	        ordered ``branch, summaries, reconverged``: ``branch`` is the

871	        booleans aligned with ``summaries`` (keys in Unicode code point
